predecessors.name: Emirate of Jabal Shammar
predecessors.text: Riyadh, 'seized from the control of the Emirate of Jabal Shammar' on 13 January 1902

successors.name: Kingdom of Hejaz and Nejd
successors.text: the Sultanate of Nejd and the conquered Kingdom of Hejaz, merged by Ibn Saud on 8 January 1926 'into the Kingdom of Hejaz and Nejd', less the Idrisid Tihamah coast (a vassal from 1926, asir dossier)

rulers.name: Abdulaziz bin Abdul Rahman Al Saud (Ibn Saud)
rulers.title: Emir of Riyadh; Emir of Nejd and Hasa from 1913; Sultan of Nejd from 1921

ledger.x: 13 January 1902: Ibn Saud takes Riyadh and the Al Saud have a state again.
1905: the rest of Najd between Riyadh and Qassim is Saudi.
13 April 1906: Qassim passes to the Saudis.
1913: the Emirate of Riyadh becomes the Emirate of Nejd and Hasa.
1913: Ibn Saud takes al-Hasa and Qatif from the Ottomans.
26 December 1915: the Treaty of Darin puts Ibn Saud under British protection.
1918: Saudi and Ikhwan forces fight the Hashemites for al-Khurma.
1919: al-Khurma goes to the Saudis.
1919: ceasefire at al-Khurma, which 'lasted until 1924'.
1920: the Saudis take Abha and the Asir highlands.
1921: Abdulaziz declares himself Sultan of Nejd.
2 November 1921: Ha'il falls and Jabal Shammar is annexed.
1922: Cliopatria adds the northern frontier lands (about 600 cells beyond Ha'il and al-Jawf).
2 December 1922: the Uqair frontier with Kuwait.
29 August 1924: Ibn Saud marches on Taif.
13 October 1924: Mecca falls, after Taif.
9 December 1925: Medina surrenders.
19 December 1925: the Kingdom of Hejaz surrenders.
23 December 1925: the Hejaz campaign ends.
8 January 1926: the Sultanate of Nejd is merged into the Kingdom of Hejaz and Nejd.

wars.name: Saudi-Rashidi war
wars.outcome: Saudi victory: Riyadh 1902, Qassim in 1906, Ha'il on 2 November 1921, when Jabal Shammar was 'completely conquered'.

wars.name: Conquest of al-Hasa
wars.outcome: Saudi victory over the Ottoman garrison in 1913.

wars.name: Khurma crisis
wars.outcome: Saudi and Ikhwan forces captured al-Khurma from the Hashemites; a ceasefire lasted until 1924.

wars.name: Kuwait-Najd border clashes
wars.outcome: Sporadic clashes over Ibn Saud's claim to Kuwaiti territory; settled by the Uqair frontier of 2 December 1922.

wars.name: Saudi conquest of Hejaz
wars.outcome: Saudi victory: Taif, Mecca (13 October 1924), Medina (9 December 1925), Yanbu and Jeddah (19 December 1925); the campaign ran 29 August 1924 to 23 December 1925.

certainty.note: Desert and tribal frontiers with no survey; the Treaty of Darin (1915) 'attempted to define' the borders of the British-protected lands but the page gives no line.
The Kuwait frontier is a straight line along the 29th parallel from 2 December 1922 and is the one sharp line; the Hejaz and northern frontiers are still undefined.
